case_scope: Supplied synthetic brief only; no case traces, route records, product-temperature readings, or verified quality outcomes supplied.

sources.title: Recommended International Code of Practice for Packaging and Transport of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables
sources.publisher: Codex Alimentarius Commission / FAO-hosted official PDF
sources.released_version: CAC/RCP 44-1995, Amendment 1-2004; official text in FAO/WHO Fresh Fruits and Vegetables (2007); no later edition asserted.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the official PDF around §2.19 and adjacent load-securing/mixed-load provisions. Confirmed that the code says between packages in the warmest area and attributes the top/side-wall/rear coordinate to recorder companies.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If available, the code recommends a small air recorder between packages where the warmest temperatures occur. Recorder-company guidance gives an example on top, near a side wall, one-third in from rear doors, away from direct refrigerated-air discharge. It does not specify an unsecured logger or a produce-core measurement.
sources.applicability: Primary transport and air-recorder placement guidance; useful for placement and documenting limitations, not proof of local practice, a product temperature, or a safe limit.

sources.title: The role of post-harvest management in assuring the quality and safety of horticultural produce
sources.released_version: FAO web text, chapter 3; publication/version date not stated on the retrieved page.
sources.locator: §3.4, especially paragraph on commodity temperature versus air; adjacent refrigerated transport and handling guidance.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the full official page and read the refrigerated transport/storage and temperature-measurement text, including surrounding airflow and loading conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: General postharvest guidance says to preserve air spaces for circulation and measure commodity temperature rather than air temperature; transport advice is conditional on produce and operations.
sources.applicability: Supports separation of product and air measurement and measurement of starting/product state; does not establish the cooperative's crop or any numeric threshold.

sources.title: Section 6: Temperature and relative humidity control
sources.released_version: Web chapter; edition/date not stated on the retrieved page; underlying cited material includes Kader 1992.
sources.locator: §6, especially heat transfer, shade, and packaging/ventilation discussion at lines 20-27; forced-air context at lines 40-61.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official page and checked the heat-transfer, shade, vapor-barrier/liner, and vent-alignment discussion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The page describes conduction, convection, radiation, and evaporation; shade is conditional on feasibility; added packaging can make cooling more difficult, and vent alignment is recommended for vented liners. Cooling methods and produce tolerance vary.
sources.applicability: Mechanism source for passive packaging and shade trade-offs; does not show that a particular liner, cooling method, or crate is appropriate here.

sources.title: Real-Time Temperature and Humidity Measurements during the Short-Range Distribution of Perishable Food Products as a Tool for Supply-Chain Energy Improvements
sources.released_version: Processes 2022, 10(11), 2286; version of record published 4 November 2022. MDPI version notes list later HTML updates, including 3 September 2025; original DOI identity retained.
sources.locator: Abstract; §§2.1-2.4 (sensors, crate mapping, route); §§3.1-3.3 and conclusions (stop, refrigeration, and cargo findings).
sources.observed_operation: Queried the exact MDPI publisher article and version notes; reviewed the publisher-indexed abstract and method/result text. Direct page open returned HTTP 429 during this review, so the full page was not directly retrieved.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Publisher text describes 18 wireless T/RH modules, mapped crate positions, five stops over 4 h 30 m, a refrigerated van route, and changes associated with door openings and operational/refrigeration conditions. Sensors represent crate-near environmental readings, not product-core or quality endpoints.
sources.applicability: Field implementation comparator for distributed crate/route monitoring and event logging. Its single route and local product/loading/weather conditions do not predict this cooperative's route.

sources.title: Thermal Management of Short-Range Distribution of Perishable Food Products Using Phase Change Materials in Packaging: Real-Time Field Data Acquisition
sources.released_version: Energies 2023, 16(13), 5191; version of record published 5 July 2023. MDPI Notes records a version-of-record PDF upload on 6 July 2023 and later HTML updates through 31 December 2025; source ID and DOI retained.
sources.locator: Publisher PDF §§2.1-2.4.3 and Tables 2-3 (crates, route, sensor setup); §§3-4, especially the crate-sensor results and PCM-reserve discussion.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and inspected the 13-page official MDPI-hosted PDF, including methods, sensor setup, route conditions, and results. The SHT30 modules are in ventilated housings and read ambient air; sensors are positioned among the produce, with a separate cargo-air sensor.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: One insulated van route in winter with refrigeration off, six unloading stops, sunny conditions and 1-10 °C reported ambient range; oranges in RT5HC PCM alveoli versus empty-alveoli controls. The sensors measure air around produce, not orange cores. The reported effect is crate-sensor temperature variation; the PCM phase change was not finished by journey end and future autonomy/quantity work is noted.
sources.applicability: Evidence of possible package-air buffering in one specific field setup. It does not establish product-core, delivered-quality, or powered-cooling benefit for the unknown cooperative case.

sources.title: Artificial fruit for monitoring the thermal history of horticultural produce in the cold chain
sources.released_version: Journal of Food Engineering 215 (December 2017), pp. 51-60; version-of-record DOI record.
sources.locator: Publisher abstract: biomimetic artificial-apple prototype and cooling comparison against ten real apples and water-filled simulators.
sources.observed_operation: Queried and read the publisher's ScienceDirect abstract and bibliographic record. Direct full-page retrieval was unavailable; the review uses the publisher abstract only, not the full article.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The prototype shell and filling were designed for a fruit of interest; the reported validation was an artificial apple during cooling against ten apples. Water-filled simulator differences were also reported. No cross-species validation is established by this abstract.
sources.applicability: Supports considering a crop-matched thermal surrogate if separately validated; it does not validate a generic simulator for unspecified produce.

sources.title: Adoption challenges of environmental monitoring practices: case study of temperature data loggers in selected Australian vegetable supply chains
sources.released_version: Applied Water Science 14, article 260 (2024); version of record published 23 November 2024.
sources.locator: Methods §4 and Findings/Discussion §§5-6; cost, mixed-product, labor, information-sharing, and accountability findings.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and read the full publisher page, including the 2021/22 study population/method and findings about adoption barriers.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Exploratory qualitative case study of three purposively selected vegetable supply chains in southeast Queensland, with semi-structured interviews and thematic analysis. Findings describe the selected cases, not all supply chains or this synthetic cooperative.
sources.applicability: Useful as a source of questions about cost, retrieval labor, mixed products, data ownership and accountability; not a local fact or general prevalence estimate.
